steps.name: Confirm CMS onboarding requirements with the EM
steps.action: Review the confirmed Windows/WSL, Visual Studio Code, required-admin and GitHub baseline. Resolve the remaining subteam questions: required access subset, repositories, permissions, runtime versions, AWS/VPN applicability and verification criteria. Record completion only after EM review.
steps.verification: EM has confirmed the team-specific plan. Optional tools are not automatically mandatory.

steps.name: Verify company account prerequisites
steps.action: With Employee Tech, confirm company identity availability, work email, Okta/MFA and access to the team's communication tools.
steps.verification: The hire signs in successfully using the approved flow. Do not store credentials in this planner.

steps.name: Prepare GitHub account and authenticator-app 2FA
steps.action: Create a GitHub account, or reuse an existing personal account, and use authenticator-app-only 2FA as specified by the GitHub setup guide. Provide the GitHub username to #helpdesk when requesting TR-AP-GitHub-CMS and any known repository team. Do not share passwords, recovery codes or tokens.
steps.verification: The hire can use the GitHub account with authenticator-app 2FA and has supplied the correct username for the access request. Organization membership and SSO are separate outcomes.

steps.name: Accept CMS GitHub invitation and complete SSO
steps.action: After Helpdesk confirms the username was added, complete https://docs.services.as24.tech/products/github/user-management/#sso-workflow for https://github.com/orgs/tdr-cms/sso. Click Continue, use the approved work-identity login and Okta MFA. Complete SSO once per organization so AD identity can match the GitHub user for team synchronization.
steps.verification: Confirm organization membership and completed SSO for the intended GitHub account. Do not record repository access from SSO alone or collect credentials in this planner.

steps.name: Verify access to an agreed CMS repository
steps.action: After the repository access request is approved, allow up to 6 hours for changes to fully sync before asking ET to verify. Then check the requested CMS repository and permission. The platform documentation describes a 90-minute team-sync cycle, but the GitHub Access guide sets the longer end-to-end window; do not retry the request just because a sync is pending.
steps.verification: The hire can access the intended repository with the requested permission. Organization membership or a completed ticket alone is insufficient.

steps.name: Review the CMS workstation setup plan
steps.action: Review the confirmed Windows with WSL and Visual Studio Code baseline. Confirm approved Windows/WSL versions, SDKs, local services and subteam-specific VPN needs. Local admin is required and requested in #helpdesk. Do not reuse the Dealertrack Oracle/IIS setup automatically.
steps.verification: The CMS subteam has supplied an approved setup plan and runtime versions. This records review, not completed installation.
steps.mode: Team review; no installer or CMS checker

steps.name: Verify Windows, WSL and Visual Studio Code
steps.action: After approved local admin is verified, follow the approved Windows/WSL setup process and configure Visual Studio Code for the agreed CMS workflow. Request admin through #helpdesk; do not bypass device restrictions. This dashboard does not install software.
steps.verification: Confirm Windows/WSL meet the team requirements, WSL starts successfully, and Visual Studio Code opens the agreed workspace using the approved WSL workflow. Record completion manually.

steps.name: Install and verify GitHub CLI through approved apps
steps.action: Use SelfService or Company Portal to install GitHub CLI for the approved Windows/WSL workflow. If it is unavailable, ask #helpdesk to add it there before installation. Do not substitute an unapproved installer.
steps.verification: GitHub CLI is available in the intended development shell; check gh --version. This records a manual check and does not authenticate or install anything from the dashboard.

steps.name: Sync the CMS repository into a home-folder Code workspace
steps.action: Create a Code folder in the approved development home folder and sync the agreed CMS repository there. Avoid Desktop, Documents and folders synchronized with SharePoint or other cloud storage. Use approved company tools and project data. Do not put customer personal data in the repository or tokens in documents/chat; ask the project lead when data rules are unclear. Follow any separately approved programme-tool setup if applicable.
steps.verification: The hire can open the intended repository on GitHub and has the agreed local checkout under the home-folder Code workspace. Request only access needed for assigned work.

steps.name: Verify a CMS dependency restore
steps.action: After approved setup, configure the agreed project feeds locally against traderca.jfrog.io and restore the agreed CMS project without sharing credentials.
steps.verification: Record a successful restore of the team-selected project; artifact login alone is insufficient.

steps.name: Verify the agreed CMS build
steps.action: Build the team-confirmed repository/branch with its documented toolchain. This dashboard does not execute a build.
steps.verification: The agreed project builds successfully with the confirmed SDK and configuration.

steps.name: Verify CMS application readiness
steps.action: Run the EM-approved CMS smoke test in an approved test environment. Confirm any required AWS, VPN, database or other access before testing.
steps.verification: The agreed application smoke test succeeds. Inventory, granted access and mock verification do not establish readiness.

confirmedRequirements: CMS GitHub organization access requires the TR-AP-GitHub-CMS Okta group; use an Access Request ticket or #helpdesk post. Organization SSO and repository access remain separate.
The workstation baseline is Windows with WSL and Visual Studio Code.
Local machine admin rights are required. Request them with a separate post in #helpdesk.

Specific CMS repository access uses a #helpdesk post or Access Request ticket. Include the repository/permission and, whenever possible, a team/AD group or example user with the needed access. Allow up to 6 hours for changes to fully sync before asking ET to verify.
AWS and VPN access depend on the CMS subteam; there is no universal CMS AWS/VPN entitlement.

GitHub setup guidance: use an account with authenticator-app 2FA, provide the username to #helpdesk, complete organization SSO after helpdesk confirmation, and use approved GitHub CLI installation and a home-folder Code workspace outside synced folders.
